plans.label: Comparative History, Culture and Global Politics
plans.concept: Study empire, decolonization, political institutions and representations of cultural identity through history, comparative politics and humanities research.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Required personal and academic development with source evaluation and academic writing.
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI

GOSHIST111.name: Modern History
GOSHIST111.contribution: Provides chronological grounding in imperialism, nationalism and decolonization.
GOSHIST111.topics: Modernity and periodization; Industrialization and reform; Political ideologies and nationalism; Migration and imperialism; National, class, gender and racial identities; World wars; Russian Revolution and Soviet history; Democracy and dictatorship; Cold War; Decolonization; Globalization; Historical visions of the future

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: Develops comparison of states, regimes, nationalism and political-economic institutions.
GOSPOLI112.topics: Democracy and authoritarianism; Democratization and democratic backsliding; States, nations and nationalism; Constitutions and courts; Executives, legislatures and bureaucracies; Political economy; Parties and party systems; Populism and technocracy; Elections and electoral systems; Political culture and polarization; Political participation; Interest groups and public policy

MCCLITR111.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
MCCLITR111.contribution: Builds close reading of narrative, symbol, genre and point of view.
MCCLITR111.topics: Definitions and value of literature; Literary genre and originality; Story, plot and narrative structure; Character, setting and point of view; Symbolism and allegory; Style, tone, humour and irony; Graphic fiction and microfiction; Creative nonfiction and memoir; Children's literature; Poetic language, imagery, sound and form; Drama and tragedy; Film adaptation

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: Develops research design and basic inference for comparative social inquiry.
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection

MCCHEAM112.name: Introduction to World Archaeology
MCCHEAM112.contribution: Uses material evidence, artifacts and settlement patterns to study past societies.
MCCHEAM112.topics: Materiality, craft and cognition; Settlement and landscape; Neolithic and Bronze Age communities; Craft production and social hierarchy; Trade and exchange; Pottery and iconography; Seals, textiles and elite identities; Domestic and urban craft spaces; Archaeological interpretation; Ancient technology and community identity; Contemporary archaeology

GOSPOLI212.name: Theory of International Relations
GOSPOLI212.contribution: Examines international order, colonialism and the roles of states and other actors.
GOSPOLI212.topics: International state system and non-state actors; Classical and contemporary geopolitics; Realism and neorealism; Liberalism and neoliberalism; Marxism and world-systems theory; Constructivism and critical theory; Foreign-policy decision-making; War and great-power competition; Colonialism and economic relations; Climate politics; UN Security Council diplomacy

MCCLITR112.name: Great Literary Works
MCCLITR112.contribution: Adds comparative world literature and analysis of colonialism, agency and narrative power.
MCCLITR112.topics: Literature, canon and world literature; Epic and heroism; Tragedy, fate and identity; Autobiography and memory; Framed storytelling and narrative power; Gender and agency; Essay and philosophical tale; Satire and irony; Colonialism and its critique; Modernist narration and subjectivity; Alienation and family; Art, sexuality and civilization; Magical realism

GOSHIST211.name: History of Empires
GOSHIST211.contribution: Compares empire formation, administration and legitimacy, including European overseas empires.
GOSHIST211.topics: Concepts and theories of empire; Imperial rise, expansion and decline; Administration and succession; Military and economic structures; Imperial ideologies and legitimacy; Culture and empire; Ancient and medieval empires; European overseas empires; Modern Asian and Eurasian empires; American power; Contemporary and future empires; Imperial legacies

MCCLITR211.name: World Myth & Literature
MCCLITR211.contribution: Analyzes how myths carry and contest cultural power across texts, images and performance.
MCCLITR211.topics: Creation and divine succession myths; Myth and cultural power; Gender and exchange; Epic and tragedy; Women, war and narrative agency; Focalization; Hero structures and motifemes; Cross-cultural storytelling; Myth in text, image and performance; Reception and adaptation; Ovid's Metamorphoses

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: Introduces concepts of social structure, colonialism, belonging and inequality.
GOSSOCI111.topics: Sociological imagination and knowledge; Social structure and socialization; Classical social theory; Colonialism and the formation of sociology; Solidarity and modernity; Identity, belonging and othering; Groups and social networks; Capital, class and mobility; Race and gender inequality; Global inequality and migration; Education and labour-market inequality

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.contribution: Supplies open-economy and growth models for reading political-economic evidence.
BENECON211.topics: Goods and financial markets; Labour markets; Phillips curve; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models; Economic growth; Saving and capital accumulation; Technological progress; Expectations; Open-economy macroeconomics; Fiscal and monetary policy; Business cycles and economic crises

MCCHEAM212.name: Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean
MCCHEAM212.contribution: Uses art and artifacts to trace long-distance exchanges, including links beyond the Mediterranean.
MCCHEAM212.topics: This course examines the painting, sculpture, and architecture of Renaissance Italy and the extensive artistic connections that linked the Italian peninsula to other regions of the world. By exploring a range of geographical contexts, from the Islamic courts of the Eastern Mediterranean and the commercial routes connecting Europe, Asia, and Africa to the newly encountered territories of the Americas, students will examine how trade, colonization, and cross-cultural exchange shaped the production and meaning of Renaissance art.

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: Investigates public policymaking across national and international scales through a globalization case.
GOSPOLI312.topics: Investigates public policy in the context of globalization. Uses a case study on sugar to examine policy‑making phases and alternative conceptualisations across national and international arenas. Students write policy memos.

MCCLITR212.name: Life & Travel Writing
MCCLITR212.contribution: Examines testimony, travel, identity and memory as culturally situated narrative.
MCCLITR212.topics: Autobiography and memoir culture; Fact, fiction and autobiographical truth; Autobiographical pact; Self and multiple identities; Individual and collective memory; Experience, embodiment and agency; Ethics and traumatic memory; Grief and disability narratives; Popular memoir and narrative technique; Digital self-presentation; Travel and spiritual self-fashioning; Migration, language and cultural identity

GOSHIST112.name: Histories of Gender
GOSHIST112.contribution: Examines gender in relation to enslavement, racialization and other institutions.
GOSHIST112.topics: Gender and intersectionality; Body sovereignty; Heteronormativity and compulsory heterosexuality; Homonationalism; Rainbow capitalism; Masculinity and sexuality; Queer ageing and memory; Slavery and racialized gender histories; Family and socialization; Health and pathologization; Media bias and book bans; Incarceration; Queer activism and resistance

MCCMEDI311.name: Media & Race
MCCMEDI311.contribution: Examines media representation and racial power, including Asian-American exclusion and incarceration as diaspora cases.
MCCMEDI311.topics: Racial construction and whiteness; Media, power and representation; Leisure, tourism and racial identity; Crime, punishment and the racialized body; Asian-American exclusion; Japanese-American incarceration; Childhood and youth; Marginalized and Indigenous storytelling; Racial extremism and propaganda; Alienation and community; Food, environment and cultural nourishment; Afrofuturism and Indigenous futurisms

MCCHEAM312.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
MCCHEAM312.contribution: Examines how modern art and museum institutions mediate cultural representation.
MCCHEAM312.topics: Modernism and avant-gardes; Cubism and abstraction; Modern architecture and design; Figuration and Mexican muralism; Abstract Expressionism; Minimalism and Pop Art; Postmodernism and conceptual art; Photography, installation, performance and video art; Globalization and contemporary art; Authorship, originality and medium; Museums, curating and reception; Eurocentrism in art history

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: Analyzes civil society, movements, migrant solidarity and public narratives.
GOSSOCI311.topics: Civil society; Social trust and social capital; Hegemony; Critical theory; Public spheres, digital publics and counterpublics; Solidarity and civil repair; Civil sphere; Social movements and intersectionality; Migrant solidarity; Civil society under authoritarianism; Decolonial critique; Public sociology

GOSPOLI111.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
GOSPOLI111.contribution: Studies political thought on nationalism, empire, race and decolonization.
GOSPOLI111.topics: Society, rights and political authority; Classical political thought; Sovereignty and political realism; Enlightenment and revolution; Liberalism and conservatism; Feminism; Nationalism; Socialism and communism; Empire, race and decolonization; Welfare state and libertarianism; Neoliberalism; Justice

GOSHIST312.name: Researching the “American Century”
GOSHIST312.contribution: Develops historical research and critical source assessment in a substantial American Century paper.
GOSHIST312.topics: Guides students through the full arc of historical inquiry, from formulating research questions to engaging critically with sources. Emphasises methodological rigour and interdisciplinary thinking and culminates in a substantial research paper.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Develops interview, ethnographic, archival and documentary approaches to cultural inquiry.
GOSSOCI212.topics: Qualitative knowledge and research design; Ethics, positionality and reflexivity; Mixed methods; Participatory research; Interview and focus-group approaches; Ethnography and participant observation; Documentary and archival sources; Visual and participatory media; Coding and thematic interpretation; Qualitative research dissemination

MCCHEAM316.name: Writing Art's Histories
MCCHEAM316.contribution: Examines the historiography and interpretive assumptions of art history.
MCCHEAM316.topics: This course examines the history of art history as an academic discipline, tracing how scholars have understood and interpreted art from the sixteenth century to the present. Through critical readings of influential texts by figures such as Aby Warburg, Erwin Panofsky, Ernst Gombrich, Michel Foucault, and Jacques Derrida, students explore the major ideas and methodologies that have shaped the field. Topics include art and history, aesthetics, meaning and interpretation, authorship and identity, and the challenges of art history in a globalized world.

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.contribution: Connects colonial histories, forced migration and identity to conflict and peacebuilding.
GOSPOLI313.topics: Conflict theories and structural violence; Identity and historical grievances; Colonialism and forced migration; International peace and security; Humanitarian law and human rights; Positive, negative and hybrid peace; Local peacebuilding; Frozen conflicts; Counterterrorism and rule of law; Transitional justice; Gender and conflict; Development and peacebuilding; Reconciliation, arts and religion; Global South perspectives; Travelling concepts and researcher positionality

findings: The nearest broad plan gives comparative work in imperialism, political economy, material culture and literary interpretation. History of Empires and Modern History overlap in imperial institutions and decolonization, while the literature and archaeology courses teach transferable interpretation and material-evidence methods. Public Policy Analysis adds globalization and governance with a dedicated case. None of these is sustained regional training. The UCR description-based historical research seminar is American Century research, not a substitute for the regional thesis.

UCR has no Hindi, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Indonesian sequence in the active workbook and limited dedicated regional history or religious study. A general politics plan or a heritage plan would shift balance without supplying that defining regional and linguistic progression. Keep the closest feasible plan as provisional evidence; full comparability and disposition await official clarification.
